messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert INC-1042: service=canary-deploy-health | severity=critical | symptom=canary 5xx ratio > 2% (us-west-2-canary-group). Page sent to SRE rotation.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert INC-1042 fired and routed to on-call (sre_rotation).

sre_sam: ack INC-1042 — oncall here, starting triage. Anyone on the canary deploy?

alex_k: I triggered a gradual rollout of v2.14.3 to 10% canary at 03:12 UTC. Noted small error spike in telemetry at ~03:18.

maria_g: Confirming — p95 latency for text-gen path jumped from 230ms -> 1.2s for canary group, and 5xx rate at ~2.3%. Seeing repeated OOM-ish traces in the sidecar logs.

ops_liz: Seeing these logs from canary pod raptor-cc-7fdc9: 
```
2026-03-14T03:18:42Z ERROR kv-cache: alloc failed: cannot reserve 512MB slab: out of memory
stack: runtime.mallocgc...
```

eng_lead_jo: tagging infra: kernel/quant-runner. Possible increased memory pressure from kv cache growth with new kernel tweak. Alex, did the change touch KV cache sizing?

alex_k: v2.14.3 includes a heuristic change to prefetch more KV pages for long context. It should be safe but increases peak memory per worker. I set --kv-prefetch=1.4x in the canary deployment.

maria_g: Can confirm memory footprint per worker is ~18% higher on canary instances vs baseline.

sre_sam: Impact assessment: affected canary group only (10% traffic). No host-wide OOM yet, but canary pods are restarting and returning 503/504s. Customer-facing error increase ~0.4% globally (small but visible on a few high-traffic customers pinned to canary).

product_toby: Noted. Which customers are on canary? Any enterprise customers impacted?

alex_k: A handful of internal test customers + some early-adopter customers — list: acme-inc, mockpay, red-ocean. I'll pull routing map.

pagerduty-bot: INC-1042 escalated: no ack from lead within 5m? (automated).

sre_sam: Already acked. Plan: 1) Pause rollout, 2) Divert traffic away from canary instances, 3) Rollback canary to v2.14.2 if instability persists. Who can run the divert command?

ops_liz: I can do traffic diversion. Recommend scaling canary down to 0 and shifting traffic to baseline pool. Command: 
```sh
# divert canary traffic
redwoodctl rollout pause --name text-gen-rollout --subset canary
redwoodctl traffic set --route text-gen --fraction baseline=1.0
```

alex_k: I'll roll v2.14.3 back once diversion confirms reduced error rate.

maria_g: After divert command, watch p95 and 5xx for global — check clients pinned to canary for lingering sessions.

sre_sam: ops_liz, please run divert and post status. I'll coordinate PD and update customers.

ops_liz: Running now.

ops_liz: Done. Commands: 
```
redwoodctl rollout pause --name text-gen-rollout --subset canary 
redwoodctl traffic set --route text-gen --fraction baseline=1.0 
```
Traffic shifted. Monitoring...

incident-bot: Deployment event recorded: rollout pause by ops_liz @ 03:25 UTC.

maria_g: Within 60s, 5xx rate fell from 2.3% -> 0.15% for the global route. P95 trending back to 250-300ms.

alex_k: I'll start rollback to v2.14.2 on the canary group and then re-enable canary at a lower prefetch ratio if needed. Command I'll run: 
```sh
redwoodctl set image text-gen canary=redwood/text-gen:v2.14.2
redwoodctl rollout resume --name text-gen-rollout --subset canary
```

sre_sam: Good. Before resume, let's capture heap profiles from failing canary pods for root cause. Maria, can you grab one?

maria_g: On it — using `kubectl exec -c profiler` to trigger heapdump.

alex_k: Rollback started. Will post when complete.

pagerduty-bot: INC-1042: Note added: rollout paused and traffic diverted by ops_liz.

maria_g: Collected heapdumps and uploaded to /artifacts/heapdumps/INC-1042/ — initial analysis shows increased resident set and a 25% higher active cache entries count tied to prefetch window.

eng_lead_jo: That aligns with hypothesis — prefetch heuristic increased sustained KV cache working set beyond expected in low-memory config. We need to add a memory cap guard on KV prefetch or adapt prefetch by worker memory.

alex_k: Rollback to v2.14.2 finished at 03:31 UTC. Canary pods now running baseline image.

ops_liz: Scaling canary back to 0 as precaution. 

incident-bot: Canary group scaled down to 0 by ops_liz @ 03:33 UTC.

maria_g: Monitoring shows 5xx back to baseline and stable. No further restarts observed.

sre_sam: I'll clear the page once we confirm impact fully resolved for 10m and tickets created for follow-up. Any customer escalations? product_toby?

product_toby: Reached out to ACME and MockPay contacts with a brief note: "We observed elevated error rates during an internal canary rollout affecting a subset of requests. Traffic was diverted and the canary was rolled back; we're investigating and will follow up with RCA." They acknowledged and no urgent SLAs breached.

pagerduty-bot: INC-1042: Alert status changed to resolved by sre_sam.

sre_sam: Marking incident as resolved for now. Follow-ups: 
- root cause: aggressive KV prefetch heuristic in v2.14.3 causing memory pressure in canary size config.
- short-term: rollback + divert (done).
- mid-term: implement memory cap on kv-prefetch, add canary mem bump during rollout, add alert for per-pod RSS increase >20% vs baseline.

alex_k: I'll open PR with conservative prefetch and memory-guard, link to heapdump artifacts.

maria_g: Adding notes to incident doc: /incidents/INC-1042-notes.md and attaching heapdumps.

ops_liz: Suggested operational checklist update: require perf sandbox run for prefetch changes before canary.

sre_sam: Thanks all — closing convo. If anything else crops up ping oncall rotation. :thumbsup:

product_toby: Thx — will include note in customer comms.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1042 resolved at 03:46 UTC. Summary: canary memory growth due to kv-prefetch; rollback and traffic diversion mitigated impact.
